strategies.name: Detect Persistence via Malicious Outlook Rules

analytics.name: Analytic 0263
analytics.guidance: Adversary uses a tool like Ruler or MFCMapi to create a malicious Outlook rule that triggers execution upon receipt of a crafted email. On email delivery, Outlook executes the rule, resulting in code execution (e.g., launching mshta.exe or PowerShell). Outlook spawns a non-standard child process, often unsanctioned, without user interaction.

tuning.description: Outlook may spawn mshta.exe, powershell.exe, or wscript.exe depending on attacker payload
Rule execution may depend on message subject, sender, or message header content
Legitimate Outlook activity should not spawn scripting or interpreter processes
Execution may occur with delay after message receipt or folder interaction

log_sources.name: WinEventLog:Application
log_sources.channel: Outlook rule execution failure or abnormal rule execution context

log_sources.name: WinEventLog:PowerShell
log_sources.channel: PowerShell launched from outlook.exe or triggered without user invocation

analytics.name: Analytic 0264
analytics.guidance: Adversary adds a new Outlook rule with modified or obfuscated PR_RULE_MSG_NAME and PR_RULE_MSG_PROVIDER attributes using MFCMapi or Ruler. Rule is triggered when email arrives, executing embedded or external code. Mailbox audit logs or Unified Audit Log shows automated rule-triggered action without user interaction.

tuning.description: Mailbox rule changes may not be captured unless advanced audit logging is enabled
Malicious rules may use spoofed or non-standard PR_RULE_MSG_PROVIDER values
Triggering emails may contain uncommon but benign-looking subjects
Target user account may be inactive or high-value (e.g., VIP, service account)

log_sources.name: m365:unified
log_sources.channel: Creation or modification of inbox rule outside of normal user behavior

log_sources.name: m365:messagetrace
log_sources.channel: Inbound email matches crafted rule trigger pattern tied to persistence logic
